- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.30) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.30), model underestimates; adjust downward by 5–10% to avoid missing upside.
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., >75% of 30d forecasts exceed true outcome by 5–15% in 3–5 day window); apply “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast 3–5 days after spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 day moving average of forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce forecast by 3–7% to align with historical volatility.
- Horizon-specific: 30d forecasts are consistently 3–8% too high in late 2024 (post-2024-12-18), likely due to sentiment overconfidence; apply 3–5% downward bias for forecasts after 2024-12-15.
- If sentiment history shows rapid reversal (e.g., +0.50 → -0.50 in 3 days), model fails to adjust; apply “sentiment lag” correction: reduce forecast by 2–5% for 2–3 days after sentiment shift.
